guideTitle: The Best Docking Stations for 4K Monitors at 60Hz
metaDescription: Many docks say 4K but only some reach 60Hz on two screens. We compared eight on 4K refresh rate, display count, DisplayLink versus native output, charging and ports.
introParagraphs: "4K support" on a dock can mean 4K at 30Hz, which feels sluggish for scrolling and moving windows, or 4K at 60Hz, which is smooth for everyday work. Check the refresh rate for each output, especially if you run two 4K monitors.

Native docks, like the Plugable Thunderbolt 4 and the UGREEN, output video directly; DisplayLink docks like the WAVLINKs use software, which works with more laptops but adds processor load. Your laptop's own display support limits native docks.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-4-dock-4k.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K output, SD and Ethernet.
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-4-dock-4k.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is the dock to choose if you want certified performance: it is Thunderbolt 4 certified, supports dual 4K or a single 6K display, and charges at up to 100W.

It has six USB ports, an SD card slot and Ethernet, needs no drivers on Mac or Windows, and Plugable lists it for M4 and M5 MacBook Air and Pro.

It was the most expensive dock here at the time of writing, and its full bandwidth needs a Thunderbolt or USB4 port on the laptop. Like every 100W dock, it won't match the charging speed of a larger laptop's higher-wattage charger.
cons: Most expensive here at the time of writing
Full bandwidth needs a Thunderbolt/USB4 port
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-4-dock-4k.bestFor: Thunderbolt and recent MacBook users who want dependable dual-display docking.
plugable-tbt-udm-thunderbolt-4-dock-4k.skipIf: Your laptop has plain USB-C; a USB-C dock like the Anker Nano costs less.

wavlink-dual-5k-4k-13-in-1.badge: Best for Two 4K or 5K Displays via DisplayLink
wavlink-dual-5k-4k-13-in-1.summary: A DisplayLink dock with 130W PD rating, dual 5K/4K output, 2 HDMI, 2 DisplayPort and Ethernet.
wavlink-dual-5k-4k-13-in-1.description:
The WAVLINK uses DisplayLink to drive two external displays at up to 5K or 4K at 60Hz, which WAVLINK lists as working across M1 to M4 Macs and Windows. That matters because many base M-series Macs natively support only one external display.

It has a 130W PD rating, two HDMI and two DisplayPort outputs, Gigabit Ethernet, five USB ports and audio.

DisplayLink requires driver software, adds some processor load and is less suited to color-critical work or gaming. Charging to one laptop is still subject to USB PD limits.
pros: Dual displays on Macs that support only one natively
wavlink-dual-5k-4k-13-in-1.bestFor: Base M-series MacBooks that need two external monitors.
wavlink-dual-5k-4k-13-in-1.skipIf: Your laptop supports multiple displays natively; the Anker Nano avoids DisplayLink for less.

wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal-dock-4k.summary: A universal DisplayLink dock with dual 4K at 60Hz over USB-C or USB-A.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal-dock-4k.description:
The WAVLINK Pro is the route to two 4K monitors on laptops that can't drive them natively: it uses DisplayLink to output dual 4K at 60Hz, and connects over USB-C or USB-A, so it works with older laptops too.

DisplayLink requires installing driver software, adds some processor load and is less suited to gaming or color-critical work. The listing summary doesn't state charging wattage.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal-dock-4k.bestFor: Laptops, including many base M-series Macs, that natively support only one external display.
wavlink-pro-dual-4k-universal-dock-4k.skipIf: You want more ports and 130W; the WAVLINK 13-in-1 adds them.

anker-prime-docking-station-4k.summary: A 14-port USB-C dock with 160W total output, dual 4K and 10Gbps data.
anker-prime-docking-station-4k.description:
The Anker Prime puts 14 ports and 160W of total output into one dock, with dual 4K display support and 10Gbps data, suited to two monitors plus drives and peripherals on one cable.

The 160W is shared across devices; standard USB-C charging to one laptop is capped at 100W. Dual display depends on your laptop's support.
pros: Most ports among USB-C docks here
cons: Laptop charging limited by USB PD
anker-prime-docking-station-4k.bestFor: Two monitors plus many USB devices.
anker-prime-docking-station-4k.skipIf: Your laptop supports only one native display; the WAVLINK DisplayLink dock works around that.

plugable-usb-c-triple-display-4k.summary: A 100W dock with three HDMI outputs: one 4K at 30Hz and two 1080p at 60Hz.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-4k.description:
The Plugable triple-display dock drives three monitors while keeping 100W charging, with support for Windows, macOS and ChromeOS.

Read the display split carefully: one HDMI runs 4K at 30Hz and two run 1080p at 60Hz. It has six 5Gbps USB ports.

A 4K display at 30Hz feels less smooth when moving windows or scrolling, so this suits three modest monitors better than a 4K setup. The listing doesn't mention Ethernet.
plugable-usb-c-triple-display-4k.skipIf: You want 4K at 60Hz; the UGREEN or WAVLINK docks provide it.

ugreen-revodok-pro-210-4k.summary: A 10-in-1 dock with 100W, dual 4K@60Hz HDMI, Ethernet and SD/TF reader.
ugreen-revodok-pro-210-4k.description:
The UGREEN 10-in-1 covers the everyday essentials for about $40 at the time of writing: 100W charging, dual HDMI at 4K 60Hz or a single 8K 30Hz display, Gigabit Ethernet and an SD/TF card reader.

Its USB-C and USB-A data ports run at 5Gbps.

It is not Thunderbolt certified, and dual-display output depends on your laptop supporting it over USB-C.
cons: Dual display depends on your laptop
ugreen-revodok-pro-210-4k.bestFor: An everyday desk dock on a budget.
ugreen-revodok-pro-210-4k.skipIf: You need three displays; the Acer 11-in-1 supports three.

anker-8-in-1-dual-monitor-4k.summary: A compact 8-in-1 USB-C hub with two HDMI, Ethernet, SD and 85W passthrough, the cheapest here.
anker-8-in-1-dual-monitor-4k.description:
The Anker 8-in-1 is a compact hub with two HDMI ports for dual 4K displays, Gigabit Ethernet, an SD reader and 85W passthrough charging.

The listing summary doesn't state the 4K refresh rate; check whether it's 60Hz or 30Hz, and on a Mac, two HDMI outputs may mirror rather than extend.
cons: Dual display may mirror on macOS
anker-8-in-1-dual-monitor-4k.skipIf: You need confirmed 4K at 60Hz; the UGREEN Revodok Pro 210 lists it for less.

anker-nano-13-in-1-triple-display.summary: A 13-in-1 dock with 100W, three displays and a detachable 6-in-1 travel hub.
anker-nano-13-in-1-triple-display.description:
The Anker Nano is two products in one: a desk dock supporting three displays via two HDMI and one DisplayPort, and a detachable 6-in-1 hub you can take with you.

It has a 10Gbps USB-C port, three USB-A ports, SD/TF reader, Ethernet and audio, with 100W charging.

Triple-display support depends on your laptop and operating system, and the detachable hub is one more part to keep track of.
anker-nano-13-in-1-triple-display.bestFor: Desk-and-travel users who want one dock for both.
anker-nano-13-in-1-triple-display.skipIf: You never travel with a hub; the Acer 11-in-1 offers three displays for less.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Plugable triple dock runs only one display at 4K 30Hz; the UGREEN, WAVLINK and Plugable Thunderbolt docks list 4K at 60Hz.
Dual 4K@60Hz needs enough bandwidth; Thunderbolt and DisplayLink docks handle it.
DisplayLink works around laptop display limits with a driver.
85W to 130W here; compare with your laptop charger.

rows: Two 4K on a base M-series Mac

faq.a: For static content, yes, but motion and scrolling feel less smooth than at 60Hz.

faq.q: Can a USB-C dock run two 4K screens at 60Hz?
faq.a: Some can, like the UGREEN, if your laptop supports it.
The WAVLINK docks list dual 4K at 60Hz via DisplayLink.
The Plugable TBT-UDM supports a single 6K display; the UGREEN a single 8K at 30Hz.

faq.q: Why won't my second 4K screen work?
faq.a: Your laptop may support only one external display natively; DisplayLink can work around that.

bottomLine: For two 4K monitors at 60Hz, the UGREEN Revodok Pro 210 is the value choice on a compatible USB-C laptop, and the Plugable TBT-UDM the certified Thunderbolt option.
If your laptop supports only one native display, the WAVLINK DisplayLink docks reach two 4K screens. Avoid the Plugable triple dock for 4K work; it runs 4K only at 30Hz.
